notes: Recorded under the owner's AFK mandate, continuing through the ranked remainder. Item 5 listed mcp-re-transport as a wholly unowned crate. Recorded by the implementing agent as routine owner-review maintenance, not as a transcription of a ruling naming this fingerprint. A MEASUREMENT CORRECTION IS PART OF THIS SLICE. The first reading of this crate counted inline cfg(test) blocks and concluded it was an EVIDENCE gap, five of nine source files having none. That was wrong. The evidence lives in tests/ — five guards in mtls_client_test.rs, four bounds in dos_hardening_test.rs, twenty framing and header controls in the lib, and a fault-injection lane whose Bazel targets are explicitly NOT manual and therefore run on every bazel test //... It is an OWNERSHIP gap over evidence that already exists, like the keysources. The corrected measurement is what this registration rests on. TWO UNITS, because the crate holds two authorities: whom this client trusts to be the proxy is not the same question as what it is willing to read off the wire, and one unit answering both would need an 'and' in its answer to ADR-MCPRE-061 section 8 question 1. EVERY EXCLUDED OUTCOME IS A DISAGREEMENT that would otherwise be resolved silently and differently at each end. A stripped CR in a header value is request splitting: the caller described one request, the peer reads two, and no error is raised anywhere — which is why the rule is REFUSE rather than sanitise, since sanitising produces a request the caller did not describe and sends it anyway. A transfer-encoding accepted alongside a content-length, or a duplicated content-length, is the classic desync. A truncated body silently shortened is a response the caller believes is complete. THE BOUNDS EXCLUDE THE OTHER SHAPE: a peer that never finishes. Catching the stall but not the trickle would leave the slower attack unbounded, which is why both directions are asserted and why the aggregate deadline exists alongside the per-read timeout rather than instead of it. PROBES M131 AND M132 red-verified. M131 needed re-adjudicating first: its anchor carries Rust byte escapes, and a TOML basic string turned them into the control characters themselves before the lane compared them, so it matched zero sites and the lane refused to run it as STALE. Rewritten with TOML literal strings. The lane refusing a probe it could not locate, rather than reporting something about the code, is the behaviour that makes a probe evidence. WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: nothing about a well-framed response being TRUE, correctly signed, or from the right peer — the RFC 9421 evidence is checked above this layer and the peer's identity is THM-0109's subject; nothing about the proxy's own framing, which is a different authority whose symmetry is by construction rather than by a shared owner; and no number is asserted as sufficient — what is claimed is that a ceiling and a deadline are applied and that exceeding either refuses.
